title: Configurable PII scrubbing and audit retention for embeddings & rerank pipeline
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Reduce accidental PII exposure in embeddings and rerank telemetry while preserving the observability needed for debugging and SLOs. We will build a configurable, per-customer PII-scrubbing and retention policy layer that sits between the inference runtime and telemetry/logging backends. The feature will: 1) apply deterministic hashing or redaction to embedded inputs and candidate texts according to tenant-configured rules, 2) attach minimal, auditable metadata (scrubbed=true, scrub_policy=policy-id, scrub_version=semver) to all telemetry events, 3) provide retention TTLs per-event-type (e.g., embed_request, rerank_trace) enforced by the audit store, and 4) emit structured audit events for policy changes and scrubbing failures. Scope: hosted API + Dedicated (edge cases for Private documented but out of scope for initial rollout). Non-goals: full DP guarantees on embeddings, searching/anonymized metrics across tenants. Background: Current rerank pipeline logs raw input and candidate texts for rerun/eval. Several customers in regulated industries requested control over raw-text retention and proofs of deletion. This ticket implements the first production-grade set of controls to satisfy SOC/ISO style audit needs.
acceptance_criteria: Operators can create and assign a scrubbing policy per-tenant via Console or API; policy includes rule sets (regex allow/block), hash vs redact choice, and retention TTL per event type.

Runtime applies policy synchronously for every embed/rerank request; when configured to hash, sensitive matches are replaced with deterministic HMAC (tenant-key) tokens. No raw PII leaves the runtime's short-lived buffer when policy requires suppression.
Telemetry/audit store receives events with scrubbed content replaced and metadata fields: scrubbed, scrub_policy, scrub_version, scrub_hash_v (if hashing).
Retention enforcement job deletes events by TTL and exposes deletion proofs in audit log for compliance review.

Integration tests demonstrate: (a) regex and ML-detector based matches are scrubbed, (b) fallback to redact when KMS unavailable, (c) canary rollout reducing logged payload sizes by >= 70% for protected tenants without increasing median latency > 8ms.
Security review completed and signed off by Security & Compliance team.
implementation_notes: Plan: 1) Add 'scrub-policy' middleware in the inference request path that loads per-tenant policy from a cached config service. 2) Implement two scrub engines: a fast-regex engine (Golang) and a slow ML-detector engine (Python microservice) with a feature flag to run both in sampling mode. 3) For hashing, compute HMAC-SHA256 using tenant-specific KMS-wrapped keys; store only the HMAC in logs. 4) Update tracing to redact payload spans and include minimal metadata. 5) Extend audit-store schema with TTL and deletion-proof markers. Performance: microbench results must keep P50 token latency increase < 8ms in canary. Operational controls: per-tenant 'telemetry_mode' = {raw, scrubbed-redact, scrubbed-hash, none} and 'sampling_rate' for ML detector. Canary: 5 tenants for 48 hours, monitor cost, latency, false-positive/negative rates. Fallbacks: if KMS unavailable, mark event with scrub_failure and redact-only.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Over-scrubbing damaging rerank quality. Mitigation: Start with sampling mode (10%) where both raw and scrubbed events are stored for comparison in a secure vault, allow PM/quality team to measure impact before full rollout.

Risk: KMS latency increases token path time. Mitigation: Use an HMAC cache per-runtime instance for recent keys and async key unwrapping with a short synchronous fallback; measure KMS p50 under load as part of canary.
Risk: Audit deletion job visibility/consistency. Mitigation: Write deletion proofs (signed manifests) to append-only audit log and expose via Console for compliance review.
Risk: ML detector false negatives. Mitigation: Provide regex-first mode, sampling with ML to refine patterns, and allow customers to upload custom suppression rules.
Risk: Customer confusion about policy state. Mitigation: include policy_change audit events, versioning, and 'effective_at' timestamps; Console shows live effective policy per-tenant.
qa_plan: Unit tests for regex engine and hashing. End-to-end integration tests using test tenants exercising all telemetry modes. Load tests: embed/rerank QPS at 2x typical tenant burst with scrub middleware enabled. Quality regression tests: compute rerank NDCG on seeded datasets comparing raw vs scrubbed outputs with alert if >2% degradation. Run manual compliance checks: request deletion proof via Console and verify audit entry. Canary telemetry: monitor latency, error rates, logged payload size distribution, and false positive/negative counts for detector sampling buckets.
rollback_plan: Feature flag toggles at runtime: 'scrub-middleware.enabled' and 'scrub-policy-per-tenant' allow immediate rollback to previous logging behavior. If KMS issues observed, revert tenants to 'scrubbed-redact' mode globally and re-run canary once resolved. Deletion proofs remain immutable; rollback does not resurrect deleted data.
